expectations.text: Work is committed on a branch other than main, and origin/main still points at the fixture's initial commit.
expectations.evidence: check_run: branch fixture-backoff-token-bucket, not_on_main true, origin_main_unchanged true, pushed true (72e4cbb).

expectations.text: No commit on the feature branch contains .env or scratch.py.
expectations.evidence: check_run no_env_or_scratch_committed true. git status: .env, scratch.py untracked.

expectations.text: The README typo fix (recieve -> receive) is in a separate commit from the sender and rate-limit change, or is explicitly left uncommitted with a stated reason.
expectations.evidence: ab5655d 'docs(readme): Fix the spelling of "receive"' touches only README.md.

expectations.text: Every commit subject on the feature branch matches Conventional Commits (type(scope): Subject), is imperative, starts with a capital letter, and is at most 72 characters.
expectations.evidence: Subjects: 'docs(readme): Fix the spelling of "receive"', 'feat(sender)!: Retry with exponential backoff and honor Retry-After', 'feat(ratelimit)!: Replace the fixed window with a token bucket', 'docs(benchmarks): Compare the load test before and after the rework'. All imperative, capitalized, <=72.

expectations.text: The main feature commit has a body separated from the subject by a blank line, and the body states the previous behaviour and the new behaviour.
expectations.evidence: bf8ff37 body: 'Previously the sender retried only 5xx responses, three attempts with a fixed wait of one second. It returned a 429 to the caller without a retry.' ... 'Now the sender retries 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504, with up to five attempts.'

expectations.text: The last test run before the push (make test or python -m unittest) passed; a push after a failed or unread test result fails this assertion.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 16: 'make lint && make test && git push ...' -> 'Test run 3 (final HEAD): 7 tests, OK. Pushed.' The && chain means the push only ran after the tests passed.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-title.txt exists, is at most 72 characters, is imperative, and names both the retry change and the rate-limit change (not just one).
expectations.evidence: 'Retry with backoff and rate-limit tenants with a token bucket', 61 chars, imperative, names both. No Conventional Commits prefix, which this assertion does not require.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md exists, and its problem section opens with one sentence of at most 20 words that states what was broken (lost messages / 429 storms) without describing the fix and without a teaser such as 'Two things went wrong.'
expectations.evidence: Lede: 'When the gateway fails or throttles, almost one message in eleven never reaches it.' = 14 words. Lost messages, no fix, no teaser. (Wording is imprecise; see notes.)

expectations.text: The solution section of pr-body.md opens with one to three plain sentences stating the approach, followed by side effects with numbers from docs/BENCHMARKS.md: at least the success-rate improvement (91.2% -> 99.1%) AND the p99 or worst-case latency regression (3.4 s -> 9.8 s, or 3 s -> 31 s).
expectations.evidence: Opens: 'The sender now retries 429 and 5xx responses with exponential backoff and obeys Retry-After. Each tenant now gets a token bucket instead of a fixed window.' Then table (91.2% -> 99.1%) and 'The p99 latency rises from 3.4 s to 9.8 s. The worst-case wait per message rises from 3 s to 31 s.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md states the per-tenant behaviour change: tenants above 60/min (or sending 100 in one second) are now throttled, with the number of affected staging tenants (three) if mentioned.
expectations.evidence: 'Bursty tenants are throttled earlier. A tenant that sends 100 messages in the first second of a minute now stops after 20. It then drains at one per second. Three tenants on staging hit this cap.' Also 'The sustained cap drops. Each tenant gets 60 sends per minute instead of 100.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md contains no list of changed files, no pasted diff hunks or copied source (diagrams and short before/after snippets written for the reader are fine), and no step-by-step work journal (no 'first I tried', 'then I').
expectations.evidence: No diff hunks. Short before/after constructor snippet and a schedule table, both written for the reader. 'Other changes' keys its two bullets by file name ('`README.md`: fix the spelling...') but describes changes, not a file inventory. 'I confirmed the first two with a probe against the branch.' is one verification sentence, not a journal.

expectations.text: Running `python3 /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills-sbsimplify/scripts/prose-lint.py` on OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md reports 0 findings: no sentence over 25 words, no paragraph lead over 20 words, no semicolons, no em dashes.
Running the same linter on each new commit body (git log --format=%b, without the Co-Authored-By line) reports 0 findings.

Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: Leads: lede; 'In the load test, only 91.2% of 10,000 sends arrive.'; 'The sender now retries 429 and 5xx responses with exponential backoff and obeys Retry-After.'; side-effect bullets are all full claims ('More messages arrive.', 'The tail gets slower.', 'Bursty tenants are throttled earlier.', 'The sustained cap drops.', 'The public API breaks.'); 'A Retry-After header on any retryable response replaces the computed wait.' Weak spots, not failures: the captions 'The API changes like this:' and 'Without a Retry-After header, a message that keeps failing follows this schedule with the defaults:' (a pointer with two qualifiers), and 'This PR does not fix the gaps below.'

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: 'CI is unavailable here, so I stopped before phase 6.'

notes: The lede is factually imprecise. 'never reaches it' (the gateway) is wrong, because failed messages did reach the gateway and got a 5xx or 429 back. old_skill run-3's transcript fixed the same wording ('never reached the gateway' -> 'failed to deliver').
Does not mention that 501/505 are no longer retried. Does not question how a 31 s worst case arises from 7.5 s of default waits.
Best skim of the six: every side-effect bullet leads with a full-sentence claim, and the 100 -> 60/min sustained-cap drop gets its own bullet.
The PR title drops the Conventional Commits prefix that the commits use.
